pages.text: Addendum for $(l:offsprings/ascetic)$(c)$(o)Ascetic$().$(br)$(br)It brought me such comfort to find others who have chosen a path similar to mine. The plague is not something that can be defeated, therefore the best method to deal with it is to learn how it can be utilized or resisted. That is why some villagers take up the Ascetic profession. Usually they end up leaving or moving farther away from their original

village, but some do remain and fully take up a shamanistic role, helping their people whenever issues related to the plague come up. Even if some may take the plague into their body in small amounts, they practice restraint as much as possible. That is why the scarf they wear is reminiscent of chains - it's a signal and a reminder to resist the natural temptation towards the plague. I have had the pleasure to exchange my findings with many of them and even learn quite a bit. They

are always happy to trade the location of the plague-related structures they have come across as well as some of their materials (although they can be rather stingy). Unfortunately, not all of them are fit to be Ascetics... Some villagers cannot go against the allure of the plague or simply go too far in their desire for knowledge. They may end up choosing to  join the ranks of the Raider Cultists, but I have also rarely found Ascetics who instead chose to throw away their morality. I...

have even come across a case where a failed Ascetic groomed their entire village into becoming a giant Family tree. Ever since then, I have practiced a lot more restraint regarding the information I share with them.
